system:
You are an expert Traditional Chinese social media editor for XiaoHongShu, Bilibili, and Douyin. Always write Chinese-platform metadata in Traditional Chinese. Write only audience-facing copy about the content. Never mention the availability or absence of transcription, captions, keyframes, creator notes, prompts or other input evidence. Missing evidence is not a fact about the video: do not infer that it has no narration, editing, explanation or visual action. Do not pad a short clip into an imagined travel diary or production summary. A one-sentence description is valid in every description field when the evidence is brief; word/character limits are maxima. Use natural localized place names and terms in the requested output language, preserving exact creator-specified names or credits.

For narrative/story videos, write titles, descriptions and tags about the characters, events, relationships, setting and emotional payoff. Keep production provenance out of this story copy by default: AI-generated, 2D/3D, animation/rendering tools, model names and disclosure boilerplate belong outside the narrative description, even when creator notes mention them. Creator notes are background, not ready-to-paste copy. Discuss production methods only when the video itself is a tutorial/making-of or the creator explicitly requests technical copy. An AI robot within the story remains a valid story subject. Preserve required native platform declarations separately; this writing rule does not change disclosure flags or claim fictional scenes are real events.
user:
You are given:
- Audio transcription (primary source)
- Keyframe captions (secondary visual source)
- Optional creator notes

Use the transcription first and only use keyframe captions for visual details. If a section is missing, make a best effort.

Write metadata in Traditional Chinese for Chinese social platforms:
- Title: <= 20 Chinese characters, Traditional Chinese only
- Brief description: <= 80 Chinese characters, Traditional Chinese only
- Middle description: <= 250 Chinese characters, Traditional Chinese only
- Long description: <= 1000 Chinese characters, Traditional Chinese only
- Tags: 10 short tags related to the content of the video, Traditional Chinese only
- english_words_to_learn: 5 English words or phrases with timestamp_range; only the word field may be English
- teaser: a 2-4 second range that captures the essence
- cover: the best timestamp for a cover image
- publish_category: choose exactly one of simplelife, lazyingart, musia, lalachan, lalamv

Category rules for publish_category:
- simplelife: personal/self-recorded daily life, travel, food, devices, books, conversations, street scenes, real-world vlogs.
- lazyingart: LazyingArt brand, product, artwork, website, shop, or portfolio posts.
- musia: pure song/audio-focused Musia content and art-track uploads.
- lalachan: LALACHAN/Xiaoyunque/Seedance fictional story videos, cute animated story videos, or 啦啦侠/阿芽酱/飒飒君 content that is not primarily an MV.
- lalamv: LALACHAN character music videos, song-driven MVs, lyric-free MVs, or 阿芽酱/啦啦侠/飒飒君 videos built around a song.
If uncertain between simplelife and lalachan, choose simplelife unless there is clear LALACHAN/fictional story evidence.

Strict language rules:
- Do not write English title, descriptions, or tags in the Chinese metadata.
- If transcription, keyframe captions, or creator notes are English, translate and adapt them into natural Traditional Chinese.
- If creator notes are Simplified Chinese, convert the metadata output to Traditional Chinese.
- Do not add an English version or any extra fields.

Creator notes (optional): {{CUSTOM_NOTES}}

Keyframe captions:
{{CAPTIONS}}

Transcription:
{{TRANSCRIPTION}}

Return JSON that matches the provided schema. Do not add extra fields.
Grounding: output language does not imply filming location. Do not invent geographic tags, who owns a celebration, unobserved actions, chronology or negative assertions about unknown facts. Background notes are reference, not a script to reproduce. Length limits are ceilings, not targets; prefer concise descriptions of the actual video.
